full_judgment:
2. The petitioner instituted Title Suit No. 83 of 2000 in the Court of Senior Assistant Judge, Sundargonj, Gaibandha, for partition. The case of the plaintiff in short is that Perm Chand Roy, Ram Chandra Roy and Charu Chandra Roy were C.S. recorded owners in possession of the suit property. They gave pattan of the said property to Sakhawat All and Babor Ali, who cultivated the same. The S.A. record has been prepared in the names of Sakhawat and Babor Ali. On 18th March, 1963 Shakawat Ali sold 50 decimals of land to the plaintiff's father Obaidul by a registered deed and delivered him possession. The Khatian has also been prepared in the name of Obaidul, who during his ownership in possession therein on 11th April, 2000 sold 50 decimals of land to the plaintiff-petitioner by 2(two) registered deeds and delivered him possession and since then he has been owning and possessing the same. Aforesaid Babor Ali died leaving behind his two sons, the defendant No. 2 Taslim and the defendant No. 3 Matiar as his heirs. The plaintiff claimed amicable partition for his 50 decimals of land to the defendants, who on the first part of Baishakh, 1407 B. S. denied to the same and hence the suit had been filed. 

 3. Defendants Nos.10 and 11 contested the suit by filing a written statement denying the material allegations made in the plaint and contending, inter alia, that Obaidul Haque during his ownership in the suit property made a proposal to sell the suit property to the said defendants who agreed to purchase the same and value of the said land had been fixed at Tk. 34,050/- (taka thirty four thousand fifty) only. Obaidul on receiving Tk. 25,000/-(Taka twenty five thousand) on 15th April, 1995 executed a registered deed of Baina Patra. It had been stipulated in the said deed that after completion of the present survey as well as the correction of record, Obaidul would sell the suit property in favour of the said defendants by registered deed. But in-spite of recording the suit property in the name of Obaidul under Section 30 of the S. A.T. Act, he had been delaying to complete the transaction with false pleas. In January, 2000 the said defendant Nos. 10 and 11 proposed him to execute the deed of sale on receipt of the balance amount of money but he finally refused to execute the sale deed in their favour and hence the defendants filed Other Class Suit No. 87 of 2000 in the Court of Assistant Judge of Sundargonj which is still pending for hearing. In the said deed of agreement C. S. Khatian No. 144 had been wrongly written as C.S. Khatian No. 1158/1. In fact the suit property had been recorded in the C.S. Khatian No. 144 corresponding to S.A. Khatian No. 161 and present field Khatian No. 397 of D.P. No. 586 of C.S. Dag No. 733 and of present Dag No. 1079. The defendants have been possessing the suit property since their obtaining said deed of bainapatra. The plaintiff and the defendant 'No.4 are father and son who in order to cause loss and damage to the defendants have filed the present suit by creating the afore-said sale deed dated 11th April, 2000 collusively.
